target.title: fix(fal): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring FAL provider request policy for media generation would not have that policy applied to FAL image generation HTTP requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

FAL HTTP config now passes `models.providers.fal.request` into the existing provider HTTP request-policy resolver. This keeps FAL on the shared provider request seam and does not change model parameters, generation parsing, or generated image parsing. Explicit private-network opt-in is now honored from the configured request policy instead of being overridden by a hard-coded deny, while the default remains deny.

## User Impact

FAL media generation requests can now honor configured request headers, proxy/TLS transport settings, and explicit private-network request policy through the existing provider request policy mechanism.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed: 44 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/fal/http-config.ts extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/fal/http-config.ts extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Resolver proof: `resolveFalHttpRequestConfig` with configured `baseUrl`, `request.headers.X-Fal-Trace`, and `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` returned `allowPrivateNetwork: true` plus the configured header and redacted Authorization header.
- Controlled real provider-path proof, using `buildFalImageGenerationProvider().generateImage()` against a local HTTP server through the normal Fal provider path:

```text
$ FAL_API_KEY=<redacted> node_modules/.bin/tsx --eval '<local Fal-compatible HTTP server + buildFalImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...) harness>'
{
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>",
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/fal-ai/flux/dev",

      "trace": "trace-harness",
      "contentType": "application/json",
      "body": "{\"prompt\":\"draw a local cat\",\"num_images\":1,\"output_format\":\"png\"}"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",

}
```

target.title: fix(ui): harden workspace file editing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared Control UI session workspace file editor landed in #104757, but several hardening gaps remained: unsaved drafts disappeared during navigation, Markdown bypassed the editor, edit capability detection was permissive, and concurrent saves could accept one stale hash through alternate file routes.

Follow-up to #104757 and #104698.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Retain every unsaved draft for the browser-tab lifetime until it is saved or explicitly discarded.
- Scope draft identity by Gateway, split pane, session, workspace root, and the canonical file path returned by the Gateway.
- Open Markdown in the same lazy CodeMirror editor as other text files.
- Show editing only when the connection has `operator.admin` and explicitly advertises `sessions.files.set`.
- Require lowercase 64-character SHA-256 CAS tokens and reject non-round-trippable UTF-16 input.
- Serialize the low-frequency save CAS sequence process-wide, covering lexical aliases and nested workspace roots before re-reading and writing.

## User Impact

Workspace files in the shared Chat session detail sheet can be edited more safely: drafts survive file/panel/session navigation, do not leak across Gateways or panes, Markdown is editable, and concurrent or stale saves fail with a conflict instead of silently overwriting newer content. Read-only and older Gateways remain read-only.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx9zc1a6mtayd31efzyxa3k0` / Actions run 29175453736: 56 gateway assertions and 62 UI assertions, including 9 Chromium editor tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx9zrrhnb1nhjvscfssfb229` / Actions run 29175625303: final 58 gateway assertions, including lexical-alias and nested-root concurrency regressions.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxa0az0cwdzxycd893vevqpn` / Actions run 29175869485: exact-head `pnpm check:changed` green across typechecks, formatting, core/UI/packages/scripts lint, dependency and policy guards, and runtime import cycles.
- Production Control UI build emitted a separate `file-editor-view` chunk (46.44 kB), preserving lazy loading.
- Fresh branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch judged correct.

AI-assisted implementation and validation by Codex.

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Loading a cron quarantine file that exceeds the safe cap now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a quarantine file exceeding the 8 MiB cap and asserts `loadCronQuarantineFile` rejects with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run` passes (47/47 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone non-test script that imports the real `loadCronQuarantineFile` from `src/cron/store.ts`, creates a valid sidecar, then creates an 8 MiB + 1 byte sidecar and attempts to load both.

Command:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101477.mjs
```

Output:

```text
=== Normal quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-normal-1783420207397.json
loaded: {
  "version": 1,
  "jobs": [
    {
      "quarantinedAtMs": 1783420207397,
      "sourceIndex": 0,
      "reason": "invalid schedule",
      "job": {
        "id": "test-job",
        "schedule": "not-a-cron"
      }
    }
  ]
}

=== Oversized quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
size: 8388609 bytes (> 8388608 byte cap)
rejected: File exceeds 8388608 bytes: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
```

The normal sidecar loads and parses successfully. The oversized sidecar is rejected before any JSON parsing or downstream cron processing occurs, with the bounded reader returning `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.

- Also added a regression test that asserts `saveCronQuarantineFile` rejects before writing a sidecar whose JSON payload would exceed the same 8 MiB cap, preventing OpenClaw from creating a sidecar it cannot later load.
